steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You're back, Zumama.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I read your letter. But shouldn't Gavial be dealing with the padishah's discovery of the Durins?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: It's not that bad. Well, not anymore.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I took a shipment of Durin ale to his court, and that kind of washed away the suspicion that the spies had planted in his mind. Now he's convinced it's just a bunch of drunkards who popped up in Acahualla and can brew decent ale.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Problem solved, then.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You're back too, High Priest.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Since when have I failed to come back after getting blown up?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You got blown up again?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Please, High Priest, don't interrupt.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: You hear that, Inam? Don't interrupt. Problem solved, everybody's happy.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You went off the rails first.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: ...Never mind.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Anyway, the ale went down so well with the padishah that he ordered Acahualla to 'start building things so it looks like people are actually living there and stop being an embarrassment to the satrapy'.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Now the Durins are busy building up their new settlement and don't have any time, so I had to call you back for the design. You think you can do it?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Zumama?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Those pretty steel buttresses by the lake...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Oh, the steel-framed sand castle.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: It's a model of the new Zeruertza that Stitch built. The Durins loved it, and they're now modeling their new settlement after it.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Wow.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Wow is right. Now, as their neighbor, we need you even more.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: What did the Tiacauh say?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: No much, other than 'Bigger!' and 'Taller!'.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: The one who wanted bigger got into a fight with the one who wanted taller.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Who won?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Neither. It was a draw.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Anyway, the Tiacauh settlement is counting on you in order to compete with the Durins.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You learned a bunch of stuff at Rhodes Island, didn't you? There's a different look in your eyes.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: What about me?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You? You're fine the way you are. You can help out when you're in the mood; when you're not in the mood, well, it's not like anyone's counting on you anyway.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: What? Did you hear what she said, girl?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Girl? Zumama? Operator Eunectes?
Eunectes does not hear a word.
She looks straight at 'New Zeruertza' by the lakeside. Perhaps she is admiring it, perhaps she is still processing the shock, or perhaps she is already thinking about competing with it.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Hmph! Well, if you put it that way, I'm not getting involved at all this time! You do whatever you want, and don't come begging for help if you screw up!
A few days later...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You're still here, High Priest? Are you not helping Zumama design the new settlement?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I said she can do it on her own this time and it's none of my business. Your memory is lousy!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You've got a long memory for grudges.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I'm a man of my word.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: But it's been a few days. Where's Zumama?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You could always check for yourself, if you're worried.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: No, na-ah, not going to happen. Your High Priest has got to lead by example.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Do you know what kind of settlement Zumama wants to build?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Wh-What kind?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Pfft.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Inam, how big of a project can Acahualla support with the resources we've got?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Well, I'm not sure how to answer that. What do you have in mind?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Bigger.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: And?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Taller.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: And?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: ...Let me think about it.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: So you didn't get an answer either!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: It needs to be bigger, and taller. Zumama said so.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I've already started gathering materials. Will you help?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I said it's none of my business.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: (Laughs) Suit yourself.
A few days later...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Good morning.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Good morning, High Priest. Are you here for a bath?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: No, just wanted to ask if the girl came to you lately.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Zumama? Yeah, she came.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: How was she? Did she come begging for help with despair in her eyes, because Inam said what she designed wasn't realistic?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Not exactly...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Then what did she come for?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Croque, I wanted to ask, why haven't the Durins built a nomadic city, with all your advanced technology?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: A what city? You mean those massive things with wheels that run around, transforming into fighting robots when they bump into enemies?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Yeah, those.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Let me think... why, indeed?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Maybe it's because there are no enemies? Or the underground railroads are too narrow?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Those are both true, but I don't think they're the key reason... Thinking, thinking... maybe it wouldn't be profitable? No, people would gladly pay for something as cool as a city that turns into a fighting robot...

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: It must be because everyone is inside the city, so they don't get to see the city transform from the outside.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Yes! That must be it!

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: What do you mean, 'Yes! That must be it'? Isn't it because there's no Catastrophes underground?

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: No what? Oh right, now I remember. People who come back from the surface say that's a thing.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: You Durins are just as unreliable as the Tiacauh—

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Wait, she's building a nomadic city?! Without me?!

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Didn't you say you weren't helping? That's what Inam said.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Th-That's none of your business!

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: But there's so much to do in order to build a nomadic city. It's not going to build itself while she shuts herself in a room, is it?

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: Yota, do you think we're spending too much time using fully automatic high-power saws? Should we spend some time working out?

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: Weren't you telling me to rest more a little while back? Hey, what's that below the high-pressure saw, it just showed up?

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: High-POWER saw.

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: No, it's the High Priest!

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: Now you're getting even worse. How did you get those mixed up?

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: It's 'high-power'. No 'r' after the 'p'.

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: I mean—

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: He means me.

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: Oh, hey, High Priest. Haven't seen you in a while.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Yes, it has been a while. I heard the girl summoned you yesterday?

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: Yeah—

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: No!

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: No?

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: We didn't see Zumama.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Then who are you cutting down trees for.

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Drop the act. More than one witness saw you meeting with Zumama. What did she say to you?

steps.name: Yota
steps.text: Oh, er, 'no man's city'!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: First, we need wood.

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: Well, if you need trees cut down, you've come to the right guys. What kind of wood you need?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: The thicker the better. Needs to bear a lot of weight.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: And don't tell anyone. Especially not the Durins.

steps.name: Yogi
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Ehm... they might not be happy about it. Better that I tell them myself.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I knew it. She's building a nomadic city.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: But why does she want wood that can bear a lot of weight? Is she trying to build a nomadic city out of wood? That's crazy.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: And what does it have to do with the Durins? They're not trying to build a nomadic city.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Wait... didn't Inam say she wanted the design to compete with the Durins'?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: A nomadic city is more impressive than buildings fixed to the ground, of course, but what the Tiacauh build won't look anywhere near as spectacular as Stitch's design...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: She's not trying to recreate that model by the lake on a mobile platform, is she? That's crazy, not even she would do that...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: But if she did...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I got to stop her! She doesn't know what she's getting herself into!

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: (Yawn) I must be hallucinating after spending too much time with the blueprints...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Who are you calling a hallucination, kid?!

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: I thought you went back to Acahualla.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: You'll lose all your hair if you keep minding things that aren't your business.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: A nomadic city? In the jungle?

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: Let me see her plans.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: (Mumbles) Don't blame me for borrowing your old homework, girl. This is for the good of everyone.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: Pretty standard stuff. When did she learn all this?

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: Do you know what these thick pipes are?

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: And are these fists that I see on the diagram?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Gun barrels and robotic arms. There are also missile pods here.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: What about residential? Where are people going to live?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Underneath the guns, storage room, cockpit. Mostly under the guns, because there are plenty of those.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: ...That wasn't really intended as a question.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I figured as much.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: I'm almost touched that she gave serious thought to commercial infrastructure and transportation...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Never mind that. I came to ask you for permission, Stitch, because this is serious.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Won't you let the girl copy your design?

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: You mean, build the exact settlement that I designed, except on a mobile platform?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I know it might be hard to accept, but—

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: My design incorporates a lot of Acahuallan elements, and the Durins and Tiacauh living together was one of the things I considered.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: If Eunectes is okay with it, it's fine by me. I'm curious to see how she puts my design onto a mobile platform.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: (Mumbles) You'll probably faint when you see it.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: But I have to ask, if Eunectes wants to build a nomadic city, why is the design basically a mobile fortress?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Let's go shopping, Zumama.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: ...I'm going back.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: It's your first time setting foot on a nomadic city. Aren't you happy about it?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I was happy. I thought it would bring me one step closer to my dream.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: But I was wrong.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: The picture etched into my memory... what I really want, is a massive construct of steel moving slowly before my eyes.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Steel walls the height of a waterfall, gleaming metal brighter than the sun, treading trees that have stood for thousands of years into dust...

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Absolute strength. Absolute power. Nothing so... mundane.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: I see. It's not beauty she's looking for; it's power.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Exactly.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: But that's not what she's like at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Hm? She spends all day chatting with the robots at Rhodes Island. They're like sisters. It's pretty cute.

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: I don't think it's arbitrary—

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Time for your checkup, Stitch! Are you coming out yourself, or do I have to come in and get you?

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: G-Gavial?!

steps.name: Minimalist
steps.text: I-I'm coming out! Don't come in!
A few days later...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Anyway, the girl wants to replicate a Durin settlement and move it onto a mobile platform.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Well, the Durin problem was coming to a head sooner or later. Fast-tracking it isn't such a bad thing, just that it's maybe a little too conspicuous.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Maybe give it a bit of polish. Make the padishah dependent on us, rather than fearful of us...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I have to say, Inam, as far as being a lord ameer is concerned, you're better than Gavial.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I'll take that as a compliment.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: How did you know all this? Couldn't resist talking to her?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Of course not. All the results of a painstaking investigation.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Anyway, now that we know what Zumama wants to do, we should help her deal with the aftermath. You can go, if there's nothing else you need.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Did you think I came to ask for help? No, I came to help you.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Follow me.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Ore vein? How did you find a place like this?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I used to live here. It turned into a mine after some geological changes.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: No wonder Zumama has a knack for finding all sorts of metals that I've never seen before.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: This is where The Big Ugly was built. It was abandoned after the girl decided to leave Acahualla.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Why did you bring me here?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Find a way to 'accidentally' discover this ore vein and offer it to the padishah. Should be enough to buy a nomadic city permit.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: That would be a bad deal, for you. The padishah would be the first to offer his support if we billed the nomadic city as a Durin brewing platform.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Deep breath, deep breath.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I appreciate it, though. It may not be useful right now, but it could come in handy in the future.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I have a question though.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Please, ask.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I've seen my fair share of eccentrics, but your mysteries might top them all.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Why did you suddenly show up with Zumama? How did you end up living with her, and even doing all this to help her?
Why?
The High Priest is used to this question from Zumama, but not from others.
Is it because Zumama was the first in the jungle to hold nuts and bolts in her hands?
Because, at heart, he is a lover of machines?
Because he was lonely for so long, and wanted someone interesting to talk to?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: When developing The Big Ugly, she said to me...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: 'We'll make this machine together, and then you'll drive it, High Priest!'

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: That's a good story.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I like it too.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Then shouldn't you be helping her with the design?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Can't go back on my word. Besides, it's high time she stood on her own two feet.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Was that anger all an act?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Burdenbeast dung—

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Yes or no?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Of course—

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: You have quite the mean streak in you. That's why you make a good lord ameer.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Alright, enough joking around. I really do think you should give Zumama a hand. I think they're almost ready to start.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Well... if you insist, I'll go back on my word, this once.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: She's not in?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Not in her room, at least.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: What about Yogi and Yota? They might know something.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: The neighbors said they went out early.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Hey, do you know where Zumama, Yogi and Yota went?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: What's Zumama doing here?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I remember this place—

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: High Priest? Inam? What are you doing here?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Worried about you—ahem, ahem.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Why are you wearing protective gear? And the direction you came from is...?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: The ruins of Zeruertza.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Why did you go there?
The dust disperses, and the High Priest sees what is in the carts behind Eunectes.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: You were picking up junk in the ruins of Zeruertza?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: It's not junk! Look, a Durin door frame! It took a ton of work to get it out from under the rubble!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: And this is part of the Great Aquapit slide. I couldn't bring the whole thing back, so I cut off the bottom part, which had the most interesting design.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: That's the definition of junk! I thought you were bringing Stitch's New Zeruertza design onto a mobile platform!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: What? Why? It's a competition. What's the point of doing what the Durins are doing?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Weren't you worried that the Durins would be unhappy?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I was going into the ruins of Zeruertza, after all. It was their home, even if it was destroyed.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: But I asked Deculture and she said I could take anything I wanted.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: The reason you had Yogi and Yota cut trees...

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I needed a decent cart to bring this stuff back.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Don't tell me you weren't planning to build a nomadic city at all?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: (Stifles laughter) How about we go back and you take your time to tell us what your plan is?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: There's no need for that. The High Priest just said it, I'm building a nomadic city.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Really.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Phew. Well, what do you have to say now, Inam?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: What do I have to say? It's not like I said anything.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Hmph. Forget that black-hearted lord ameer; how do you plan to build a nomadic city? With this junk that you dug up from underground?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Yeah, but that's not important. What's really important is—

steps.name: Strange Machine A
steps.text: Model R3-E3 Assistant Robot #0332, reporting in.

steps.name: Strange Machine B
steps.text: Model R3-E3 Assistant Robot #0719, reporting in.

steps.name: Strange Machine C
steps.text: Model R3-E3 Assistant Robot #0086,

steps.name: Strange Machine C
steps.text: rererereporporpor—

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: So you went to save your friends...

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Not entirely.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Here's what I think. The nomadic city of the Tiacauh needs to be ahead of its time. It needs to be incredible.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: As far as design is concerned, I could never compete with Stitch.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: That's why I'm building a living city.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: My friends here, once fixed, will become the building blocks of the new city.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: The robots will be your city's building blocks? And then?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Three friends make one large unit, and five large units make one huge unit, unit after unit, until they're the size of a nomadic city!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: That way, you can get an answer no matter which part of the city you talk to, and the whole nomadic city will be friends with the people living inside it!

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Okay... where will the people live?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Don't worry, I've thought about it. Here are the blueprints.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I'll just look past the multitude of problems right now. Problem after problem, yet somehow it might just work.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I think it'll work.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: First, though, you need to tell me what's going on with this shape.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: It's absolute madness. One domed roof, three pairs of wheels, medical equipment...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: A city-sized—

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Lancet-2?!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: She makes a cute big sister, doesn't she?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Look at the last page of the plans.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I've got everything thought out. A supercomputer in the center of the city, controlling all the robot friends.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I made the connector round so that Lancet-2 can sit in it—

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: What about me?!

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Didn't you give a single thought about me when designing this city?! After all the worrying I did for your sake?!

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: You know what, screw it, do whatever you want, it's none of my business, I'm going on a long trip—

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Your room's here, High Priest.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: What's this? Way out in a corner? This isn't the least bit cool compared to that round supercomputer connector! And it's right next to a warehouse—

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: That's my bedroom.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: You'll be right next door to me. You can come visit any time.
High Priest is at a loss for words. Inam can no longer stifle her laughter.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Well, how about it? Will you help Zumama or not?
Finally, the High Priest comes to terms with his emotions and composes himself, even finding the wherewithal to give his ridiculous glasses a little pompous push.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Of course I'm helping.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: First step will be a trip to Rhodes Island on your behalf.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: For what?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: To ask the subject of your blueprints...

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Whether the robot who won't even let you drink coffee will let you do this.
